cards.name: retire-the-atomic-split-k-then-stream-the-weights-past-l1-quantized-gemm-gfx950-both
cards.description: Decode-weighted block-scaled fp8 GEMM: deterministic split-K reduce for the atomic combine, L1-bypass weight hint, BLOCK_N=128, fp16 partials: 1.45x weighted
cards.key: fp8 e4m3 block-scaled a8w8 GEMM whose split-K epilogue combines atomically, decode-weighted case mix on gfx950 (skinny-M decode dominant, one large-M prefill bucket)
cards.effect: 1.4525x weighted (ratio-of-sums) director-verified against the frozen baseline, correctness pass on all 6 workload cases and all 6 oracle records; per case decode M=64 1.556x (80.6% of the weight) and prefill M=1024 1.149x; unweighted geomean 1.3464x
cards.roofline: decode: grid-underfilled latency-bound at ~1 wave/SIMD and ~63% CU coverage -> memory-bound at ~100% of the machine's measured streaming rate (a cross-case control on the same weight stream agrees within 1%), measured per-case ceiling 1.85x. prefill: compute-bound at ~20% of fp8 peak, ~3.7x above its own memory floor
cards.title: Retire the atomic split-K, then stream the weights past L1
cards.lever: When a block-scaled fp8 GEMM's split-K epilogue accumulates atomically into an output that has to be zeroed first, try replacing the atomic combine with a deterministic two-stage reduce over an explicit partials buffer (this also deletes the per-invocation zero-fill and the accumulation-order risk), then put an L1-bypass cache hint on the streamed weight operand and only then widen the N tile: the tile was neutral-to-worse until the weight stream stopped thrashing L1.
cards.apply: One constexpr each for the cache hint, BLOCK_N, SPLIT_K and the partials dtype, plus a second reduce dispatch; narrow the partials to fp16 behind an env escape hatch that restores fp32. Route large-M to a separate unmasked dense macro-tile (128x128x128, GROUP_M=4 L2 swizzle, num_warps=4, waves_per_eu=2) gated on exact 128-divisibility of M/N/K, so off-workload oracle shapes fall through to the masked path.
cards.stack:
total 1.4525x weighted, director-verified = two directions hand-merged on a shape dispatch (skinny-M decode arm / large-M prefill arm)
  - 1. decode weight-streaming (deterministic split-K reduce + L1-bypass weight hint + BLOCK_N=128 + fp16 partials) - 1.2799x weighted standalone (round 1, verified), 1.556x on the dominant decode case - carries the win
  - 2. dense prefill macro-tile (num_warps=4, waves_per_eu=2, GROUP_M=4) - 1.0426x weighted standalone (round 1, verified), 1.149x on the prefill case
  - note: the arms touch disjoint shape buckets, so this merge was additive rather than incremental; two later rounds added a further +0.44% attributable on the prefill buckets that stayed inside the metric's noise band and was not banked.
cards.verify: A/B in the scored cache-flushed window rather than on a warm profiler median (a rival candidate won the warm median and still lost the score), and confirm the zero-fill dispatch has dropped from one call per invocation to one per trace.
cards.pitfall:
Widening the N tile further to halve the redundant A re-reads regressed -> the grid is (N-groups) x SPLIT_K, so a wider tile drops the workgroup count below the streaming-rate knee -> a traffic-identical NGROUP=2 control cost the same, proving grid collapse rather than accumulator pressure; buy A-traffic somewhere other than the tile.
bf16 split-K partials failed parity outright while fp16 passed -> the partials buffer is the accumulation-order-sensitive operand -> ship fp16 with the fp32 env switch and re-read the eager error margin, which fp16 widens by roughly 10x against the gate.
A hand-rolled streaming probe 'proved' decode was already at the cold-read wall -> it measured its own ceiling, about 0.7 of the real kernel's achieved rate -> price the roof with a cross-case control on the real kernel (same weight stream, one M value against another), not a synthetic probe.
A cache-policy pairing read as a 3.9% win once and evaporated on repeat -> the scored window carries about +/-2% run-to-run spread -> never bank a single reading.
A sub-1% prefill change was unresolvable in the full-run weighted number -> an 80.6%-weight decode bucket with about +/-3% spread swamps it -> score it on its own buckets with interleaved control/patched pairs, using an env flag as the control so both arms are the same binary.
Two directions each authored the kernel source from empty, so their diffs conflicted 100% -> textual conflict, not strategic conflict -> hand-merge on the shape dispatch instead of stacking diffs.
cards.caution: Also verify the hint and the dense gate actually engaged (the divisibility gate silently falls back), and also verify K-loop unrolling from scratch after these land: a large early unroll win reversed into a regression once the byte-in-flight problem was fixed.
